Confirmed P2 from the independent review (reproduced with scratch probes): the reconnect wait depends on the OLD attached PID staying alive, but a Claude Code update respawns idle sessions onto the new binary with a NEW PID about 15 s after the service restart (~/.claude/daemon.log: 'adopted=2' then 'post-takeover prewarm burst — respawned 1/2 stale workers'; in workflow-guardrails-001 the ui lane's PID at the freeze differs from its launch). After a respawn attach-one fails: (A) exit 1, then a row without PID, then a row with a new live PID -> RuntimeError 'No live native PID' after one attach; (B) exit 1 then a listing failure -> re-raised; (C) exit 0 (`claude attach` prints 'Session <id> has exited.' and exits 0 when its probe finds no handle during the respawn) then the row with a new live PID -> returns silently, pane dead, no message; (D) exit 1 then the row still listing the old dead PID -> 'Native process is unavailable; refusing implicit restart'. Only a new live PID at the very first look reattaches.

Fix, as the reviewer proposed: stop requiring the old PID to be alive before waiting. Wait whenever this background id was verified live and attached before and no stop is recorded. (1) After an attach ends, a live row whose PID differs from the attached PID is a respawn, not a detach: reattach even after exit 0, because an operator detach never changes the PID. (2) Treat as a gap bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT: a failing listing (any exception from inventory(), including TransientInfraError, classified by type), a row still registering its PID, 'Session is not attachable', or a row still listing the old dead PID (only within a short grace, about 30 s from when the loss was seen). Keep refusing at once when a successful listing no longer lists the id, when the row's state is terminal (stopped/failed), for identity refusals, and for a first attach. Nothing is ever attached without a verified live row.
Also fix these P3s from the same review: call recorded_stop() again right after observe(), immediately before each `claude attach`, and exit on a marker there too (shrinks the race with the controller's freeze); for an unconfirmed stop intent word the message as 'The controller is stopping <node> (requested at <time>, not yet confirmed); not attaching. Inspect it with `claude logs <id>` or `claude attach <id>`.' and say so in the RUNBOOK; keep the last listing/refusal error and append it to the give-up message ('last error: …').
Tests (inject sleep/clock; patch subprocess.run and inventory as AttachOneTests does): the four respawn cases A-D now reattach the same background id; exit 0 with a changed PID reattaches; the old-dead-PID grace expires into the refusal; a vanished id and a terminal state still refuse at once; the stop re-check before attach; the unconfirmed wording; the give-up message carries the last error. Add a RUNBOOK line that an update respawns idle sessions onto the new binary ~15 s after the restart and attach-one follows them. Worker and native reviewer `claude --bg` sessions now get the auto-updater setting through their arguments. It is committed on fix/bg-settings as 98ab3f5, in the worktree /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-bg-settings. Nothing was checked against a live Claude session; the integrator's one live check is still to come.

Why this was needed: the `--bg` helper only hands the session to Claude Code's background service. The service starts the session with its own environment plus an allowlist of the helper's variables. So the helper's DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 reached a session only when the controller itself had started the service.

What changed:
- `workflow/sessions.py`: one value, `AUTOUPDATER_OFF = {"DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1"}`, now used by both `claude_env` and a new helper, `background_settings()`. The helper returns `["--settings", json.dumps({"env": AUTOUPDATER_OFF})]`.
- `workflow/interactive.py`: the worker launch and the native reviewer launch both add `*background_settings()` directly after `--name <name>`. `--settings` takes exactly one value, so the reviewer prompt still follows `--permission-mode dontAsk`. Neither launch passed `--settings` before, so there was nothing to merge.
- `workflow/pipeline.py`: preflight's base list of required CLI flags now includes `--settings`.
- The launch helper's own environment handling is unchanged: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 is still set and HERDR_* variables are still removed.

Checked against `claude --help` (2.1.281) and, statically, the installed bundle:
- `--settings` accepts a file or a JSON string. A value that starts with `{` and ends with `}` is read inline.
- These are the "flagSettings" source. Its `env` is merged key by key over the user's settings and applied to the session's environment.
- The updater checks `process.env.DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`.
- `--safe-mode` does not drop this source; only `--setting-sources` and `--restricted` narrow the sources, and the help says `--settings` still applies under `--restricted`.
- The background dispatch carries argv into the session, keeps a JSON `--settings` value as-is, and keeps `--settings` when a session restarts on a new version. Its env allowlist does not include DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER.

Docs:
- The RUNBOOK operator-boundaries bullet now says how each process gets the setting. Processes the controller starts itself (print reviewers, the challenge job, attach, the `agents` and `stop` calls, the `--bg` helper) get the environment variable. Worker and native reviewer sessions get `--settings`, merged over the operator's own settings. Preflight refuses a CLI without `--settings`.
- The practice of updating between runs and restarting stale sessions is kept.
- The README's line on `sessions.py` now mentions `background_settings`.

review.notes:
I found no P0, P1 or P2 problems. The fix works in the real scenario, not just in the unit tests. Here is what I checked in the installed Claude Code 2.1.281 binary (strings only, nothing run):

**The setting reaches the worker and reviewer sessions**
- `--settings` is one of the flags `--bg` knows takes a value. Its JSON value is therefore not mistaken for the prompt.
- The `--bg` helper passes the flag through to the session unchanged, and nothing refuses `--settings` together with `--bg`.
- The flag is also kept in the saved flags the service uses to restart a session. So the setting survives the service restart (and session respawn) that an update causes. `--settings` is on the allowlist for those saved flags.
- In the session, the `env` from `--settings` is copied into the process environment early at startup, before the workspace trust check.
- `--safe-mode` does not block it. Settings from the command line are always loaded, and the step that applies their `env` has no safe-mode check.
- These settings take precedence over user, project and local settings; only managed policy ranks above them. So the RUNBOOK's "merged over your own settings" is accurate.
- The session's auto-updater and plugin auto-update both check `process.env.DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`. With the setting applied, both stop.

**Call sites and the preflight**
- There are only two `--bg` launch sites, `interactive.py` `run` (worker) and `run_reviewer`, and both now use `background_settings()`.
- No launch passed `--settings` before, so there was nothing to merge.
- The flag sits right after the `--name` value. Neither the variadic `--tools`, `--allowedTools` and `--add-dir` flags nor the prompt position is affected.
- The preflight's `claude --help` check in `pipeline.py` main is the only one. It now requires `--settings` in both manual and automatic modes. The installed CLI lists it.

**Regressions: none found**
- The `launch()`, `reconcile` and settle paths are untouched. A session is still launched at most once, a helper that ran is never retried, and the helper's environment is unchanged (still stripped of `HERDR_`, still with the auto-updater off).
- The plan digest and receipts do not include the command, so old run directories are unaffected.
- The operator command outputs are unchanged.
- Sibling branches: fix/attach-respawn and fix/review-wait edit different RUNBOOK paragraphs and different parts of `interactive.py`. fix/lane-repair has no commits yet.

**Tests**
- The new tests parse the JSON rather than matching strings.
- They cover the manual worker, the automatic worker and the native reviewer.
- They also check that the helper still runs with the auto-updater off and without `HERDR_` variables, and that the prompt stays last.
- Both new tests fail without the change (see the scratch-copy check under tests run).
- The preflight test uses a stand-in `claude` on PATH with HOME in a temporary directory, so it makes no real Claude call.

**Out of scope**
The operator's own long-lived sessions (`md-manager-71` and the others named in the issue) can still reinstall Claude Code. The RUNBOOK's advice to restart stale sessions and update between runs still applies to them.

decisions: A listing that answers but does not list the id is still a gap while the attached process is alive; it is refused at once only after that process has ended. This keeps the existing behaviour and test (an empty listing while the process lives is waited out), and 'keep refusing at once' was read as keeping today's refusal.

Terminal states are {stopped, failed}, the two named in the assignment and the pair Claude Code itself groups as terminal. Any other state that is not attachable (starting, resuming, adopted, crashed while respawning) is a bounded gap, which is safe because nothing is attached without a live row that passed the identity checks.

The 30 s dead-PID grace starts when attach-one first sees a row listing an ended process, and resets when a live row appears. Starting it from the end of the attach would call the injected clock more often for nothing.
Any listed PID whose process has ended (reaped, or a zombie that locate's kill(pid, 0) still answers for) gets the grace, not only the exact old PID.
An interrupted attach (exit 130 or SIGINT) still ends attach-one without looking for a respawn; only exit 0 and a lost connection check for a changed PID.

After exit 0, a gap (for example a failing listing) waits until a row shows whether the PID changed, instead of returning at once. So an operator detach during a service outage prints a retry line, and could end with the give-up after 30 attempts, rather than exiting quietly.

An attach that held ATTACH_STABLE_SECONDS now resets the failure count however it ended, not only on a non-zero exit. Otherwise respawns after exit 0, one per update, would build up towards REATTACH_LIMIT over hours.

'last error' also records the attach's own failure ('`claude attach` exited 1', or the OSError) besides listing and refusal errors, so the error named is always the latest one. It is omitted when there is none.
An unconfirmed stop shows the raw node name and the background_id from the stop marker. save_json writes the marker atomically, and the id is recorded there before `claude stop` runs.

I did not touch the RUNBOOK command-table summary line (about line 343) or the auto-updater sentences (line 407), to avoid merge conflicts with fix/lane-repair and fix/bg-settings. The detail is in the attach-one paragraph (line 139).

problems.description: In a very common real case the fix still leaves the pane dead after a respawn. The branch treats "a successful listing without the id once the attached PID ended" as a session that is gone and refuses it at once. That is what the assignment asked for, but the assumption behind it is wrong. Claude Code 2.1.281's `claude agents --json` builder (printAgentsJson in the shipped claude.exe) is called without `--all`. It skips a background row that has no live process record unless the row's state is `working` or `blocked`: `if(!s&&!e&&r!=="working"&&r!=="blocked")continue`. An idle background session is listed as state `done`: Cf maps status idle to `{state:"done",tempo:"idle"}`, and done with a non-active tempo counts as settled. Settled or idle sessions are exactly the ones respawnIfIdleStale respawns. So during the respawn gap (old process shut down and reaped, new one not registered yet) a `done` lane is missing from the listing entirely, rather than listed without a PID as in case A. observe() then sees row None with the attached PID dead and raises `Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart`. This is the dead pane the issue asks to remove. The gap falls right after `claude attach` ends, because the attach ends when the old process exits, so it is the most likely thing attach-one sees next. The new test test_a_vanished_session_or_a_terminal_state_is_refused_at_once locks this behaviour in.
problems.failure_scenario: The ui lane has finished its turn and sits idle (state `done`). An update restarts the service. attach-one's reattach is delayed, or races the ~15 s prewarm burst, which respawns the session. `claude attach` exits 0 ('Session <id> has exited.') or 1, and ~0.5 s later `claude agents --json` returns without 28930c4a because no process is registered yet. attach-one exits 1 with 'Blocked: Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart', while the session comes back seconds later under a new PID. Reproduced with a scratch probe using the AttachOneTests fakes: inventory [[row(pid=old,state=done)], [], repeat(row(pid=new,state=done))] with exit 0 or 1 raises 'Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart' after one attach.
problems.fix: Once the id was attached and its attached process has ended, treat a successful listing without the id as a gap bounded by the same DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS window as ProcessEnded, e.g. raise ProcessEnded or a sibling class with the 'Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart' message and share dead_since. Refuse after the grace, as the dead-PID row does. Nothing is attached without a verified live row, so this is safe. A session that really ended is still refused, after 30 s instead of at once. Change test_a_vanished_session_or_a_terminal_state_is_refused_at_once so the vanished case is refused after the grace, add a respawn subcase E: exit 0/1, then [], then the new PID reattaches. Update the RUNBOOK list of refusals to match. An alternative is to have attach-one list with `claude agents --json --all`, so the done row stays listed without a PID and falls into the existing no-PID gap. That changes the shared inventory() and is more invasive.

problems.description: A row that stays listed without a PID after the attached process ended is now waited out for the full REATTACH_LIMIT: 30 attempts, about 274 s. This row is a working/blocked session the service retired or that crashed; the live `claude agents --json` currently shows two such rows, e31d14be and 6c3f0825. While it waits, attach-one prints 'The background service does not list ui (…) yet', but the service does list it. It ends with 'Gave up reattaching … the session may still be running', which is wrong. Before this branch it was refused at once. The RUNBOOK's list of refusals does not mention this case. This follows the assignment's 'bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT' wording, but the message and duration mislead the operator.
problems.failure_scenario: The ui lane's process crashes while attached, and the row stays listed as `blocked` with no pid. The pane prints about 29 'does not list ui yet; retrying' lines over ~4.5 min, then 'Blocked: Gave up reattaching ui (…) after 30 attempts in a row; the session may still be running. … last error: No live native PID; reconcile session before attaching' (confirmed with a scratch probe).
problems.fix: Once the attached PID is dead, bound a no-PID row by the same DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS window from when the loss was seen, then refuse with the locate error. Word the waiting line for a listed-but-PID-less row separately, e.g. 'lists <lane> (<id>) without a process yet'.

problems.description: An operator detach (exit 0) that coincides with a listing outage is now waited out for up to REATTACH_LIMIT attempts. It prints retry lines and exits 1 'Gave up reattaching …'. Before, attach-one returned quietly, because the attached PID was alive. A respawn always ends the attached process (upgrading → shutdownWorker, new spawn only after exit), so after exit 0 a still-alive attached PID already means detach without any listing.
problems.failure_scenario: The operator presses Ctrl+Z while `claude agents` is failing (the CLI is missing during an npm reinstall). The pane keeps printing 'The background service does not list ui … yet' for ~5 min, then exits 1 with 'Blocked: Gave up reattaching …' (confirmed with a scratch probe).
problems.fix: After exit 0, return at once when process_alive(attached['pid']) is true, as the old code did. Keep waiting for a row only when the attached process has ended.

problems.description: The new RUNBOOK sentence says the update 'respawns each idle session onto the new binary'. In the daemon, only idle stale sessions with no attached client are respawned: respawnIfIdleStale returns reason 'attached' when attachers>0, which is the 'N refused' in daemon.log. A pane that attach-one reattached before the ~15 s burst keeps its session on the old binary until it is detached. 'A row still starting' names a state `claude agents --json` never lists for background rows (it lists only working/done/failed/stopped/blocked). The refusal list also omits the PID-less-row give-up, and would need the grace from the P2 fix.
problems.failure_scenario: An operator reads that every idle session is respawned ~15 s after an update, and expects their attached pane to move to the new binary. It stays on the deleted binary until detached.
problems.fix: Say 'each idle session no pane is attached to'. Drop 'a row still starting'. Keep the refusal list in step with whatever the P2/P3 fixes decide.

problems.description: The message for an unconfirmed stop takes the background id only from the marker (`intent.get('background_id')`). A marker that is unreadable, or that lacks the key, prints `claude logs None` / `claude attach None`.
problems.failure_scenario: A hand-edited or damaged <node>.stop.json produces 'Inspect it with `claude logs None` or `claude attach None`.' save_json is atomic, so the controller never leaves a partial marker.
problems.fix: Fall back to the receipt's background_id (<node>.interactive.json), or drop the inspect hint when the id is unknown.

review.notes:
Verdict: problems. I found one P2: a respawned idle lane can still be refused at once. The other findings are P3.

Branch fix/attach-respawn is one commit, f6db1f1, on top of 2834604. It touches workflow/interactive.py (observe, attach_one, recorded_stop, the new stop_reported), workflow/test_interactive.py and a single RUNBOOK paragraph. None of its hunks overlap fix/bg-settings (interactive.py imports and launch code, RUNBOOK line 404, InteractiveTests), fix/review-wait or fix/lane-repair, so merges should be clean. The commit ends with the required Co-Authored-By line, and the worktree is clean.

**What the branch gets right:**
- Cases A–D reattach the same background id.
- Exit 0 with a changed PID reattaches.
- A row that keeps listing the dead PID, reaped or a zombie, is refused after the 30 s grace.
- `stopped` and `failed` rows, identity refusals and a first attach still refuse at once.
- The stop is read again right before each `claude attach`.
- The unconfirmed-stop wording and the give-up message's 'last error' match the assignment.
- Nothing is ever attached without a verified live row: locate needs an int PID that answers kill(pid, 0), and process_alive rejects zombies.
- An interrupted attach (130 / SIGINT) still ends attach-one.
- The new tests fail on the base code.
- attach-one never launches or stops a session, so the launch-at-most-once and no-stop guarantees are untouched.

**The P2 is a false premise in the spec.** The assignment assumed a respawn's gap shows up as a row without a PID. The installed CLI's own `claude agents --json` builder (no `--all`) instead drops a row with no live process unless its state is `working` or `blocked`. An idle background session is listed as `done` (status idle maps to done/idle). That is exactly the kind of session the update's prewarm burst respawns, so during the gap a `done` lane is missing from the listing altogether. The branch then refuses it at once with 'Session unavailable', as the assignment asked, but that leaves the pane dead in the real scenario.

The recommended fix is to put a missing id, after the attached process ended, under the same DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS window as the dead-PID row. This is a decision for the orchestrator, because it goes against the assignment's 'keep refusing at once when a successful listing no longer lists the id'.

**Race the fix cannot close:**
- The daemon shuts the old worker down gracefully (SIGTERM only after 5 s).
- If `claude attach` exits 0 while the old process is still shutting down, the listing can show the same live PID.
- attach-one then takes it as an operator detach and returns quietly.
- This cannot be told apart from a real detach with the data available.

**Outside this branch:** pipeline.stop_session raises 'identity changed after stop intent' if a respawn changes the PID between the stop intent and `claude stop`. That is controller code, so it is only noted here.

fix.summary:
I fixed the P2 in commit 63c69c5 on fix/attach-respawn, in /home/agentops/dev/mdm-fix-attach-respawn. The reviewer's claim is real. I checked it in the installed claude.exe (2.1.281). printAgentsJson has `if(!s&&!e&&r!=="working"&&r!=="blocked")continue`, so without --all it skips any row with no process record unless the row is working or blocked. The state mapping A() lists an idle session as `done`, so it is skipped. During a respawn gap, a `done` lane is therefore missing from `claude agents --json`, not listed without a PID. Before this fix, attach-one refused that case at once with 'Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart'. The new test case E reproduced that refusal before the code change.

The fix is in observe() in workflow/interactive.py. The id must have been attached before and its process must have ended. If a successful listing then leaves out the id, observe() now raises ProcessEnded('Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart'). attach_one already had a ProcessEnded path that waits for DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS (30 s) and then re-raises, so this reuses it with the same dead_since. A missing row and a row still listing the dead PID count toward the same 30 s. These still refuse at once: a first attach with no row, a stopped or failed row, and every identity refusal. A listing without the id while the attached process is still alive stays the existing gap, bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT. Nothing is attached without a verified live row. I updated the ProcessEnded docstring, the DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS comment, the observe docstring and the grace comment in attach_one.

Test changes in workflow/test_interactive.py:
- test_a_session_respawned_under_a_new_pid_is_reattached: added case E for exit 1 and exit 0 (the lane listed as `done`, then no row, then the new PID); both reattach the same background id.
- test_a_row_that_keeps_listing_the_ended_pid_is_refused_after_a_grace is renamed test_an_ended_process_with_no_new_one_is_refused_after_a_grace. It now covers the dead PID (reaped and zombie), a listing that keeps leaving out the id (exit 0 and 1), and the two alternating. Each is refused after the same backoff: 2, 4, 8, 10, 10.
- test_a_vanished_session_or_a_terminal_state_is_refused_at_once is renamed test_a_terminal_state_or_a_first_attach_is_refused_at_once.
- test_a_session_gone_without_a_recorded_stop_is_refused_once runs through main() with the real clock and sleep, so it now sets DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS to 0.

In workflow/RUNBOOK.md, the attach-one paragraph now lists the 30 s wait for a listing without the session, and the refusal list is updated to match.

decisions: The P2 is real. I checked it in the installed claude.exe 2.1.281: printAgentsJson skips a row with no process record unless it is working or blocked, and the state mapping A() lists a settled idle session as 'done'.

I used the reviewer's first option: raise ProcessEnded with the 'Session unavailable' message and share dead_since and DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS. I did not switch inventory() to `claude agents --json --all`, because that changes the shared inventory() used by the controller and other branches.

The grace applies only when the id was attached before and the attached process has ended. A listing without the id while the attached process is still alive stays the existing gap, bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT. A first attach with no row is still refused at once, and a test now covers that.

A session that really ended (a crash, or /exit in the pane) is now refused after about 30 s instead of at once. During that wait the pane prints the existing 'does not list <lane> (<id>) yet' lines. The reviewer accepted this trade-off.

The existing main()-based refusal test runs with the real clock and sleep, so it now sets DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS to 0 rather than sleeping 34 s. The new grace test injects the clock and sleep and covers the wait itself.

problems.description: This is a regression from 2834604. At 2834604, a detach (exit 0) while the listing failed or omitted the id, with the attached PID still alive, ended attach-one quietly. Now, after exit 0, `ended` stays "detached" through every SessionGap until a row shows up. So a Ctrl+Z during a listing outage prints "The background service does not list <lane> (<id>) yet; retrying…". If the outage outlasts REATTACH_LIMIT, it exits 1 with "Blocked: Gave up reattaching … last error: …". The same-PID-means-detach rule already covers this case: the old process is still alive, so the session cannot have been respawned.
problems.failure_scenario: Scratch probe with the AttachOneTests fakes: attaches [exit 0], inventory [[row], then TransientInfraError forever]. At 2834604 this returned None at once. Now it sleeps 29 times (about 274 s) and raises 'Gave up reattaching ui (11111111) after 30 attempts…; last error: inventory unavailable', so main prints 'Blocked:' and exits 1. With a short outage, [[row], error, [row]…], it returns after one spurious 'does not list … yet; retrying in 2s…' line.
problems.fix: In attach_one, when ended == "detached" and observe raised a plain SessionGap (not ProcessEnded) while process_alive(attached["pid"]) holds, return quietly as before. A respawn only shows once the old PID has ended, and that case is a ProcessEnded or a row with a different PID. Add a subtest to test_a_detach_ends_attach_one_quietly for exit 0 followed by a listing failure.

problems.description: There is an inconsistency in how long attach-one waits once the attached process has ended. A listing without the id, or a row still listing the dead PID, is refused after DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS. A row without a PID ("No live native PID") is waited out for the whole REATTACH_LIMIT instead, about 274 s, and ends with "Gave up … the session may still be running". Without --all, `claude agents` keeps a `working`/`blocked` job without a process record as a row without a PID. So a worker whose process crashed mid-turn waits ~4.5 minutes and gets a misleading give-up message. At 2834604 it was refused at once. The RUNBOOK says "an ended process with no new one listed after 30 seconds" is refused.
problems.failure_scenario: Scratch probe: exit 1 while the attached process is killed, then the inventory repeats [row(pid=None)]. The result is RuntimeError 'Gave up reattaching ui (11111111) after 30 attempts in a row; the session may still be running…; last error: No live native PID; reconcile session before attaching' after 274 s of sleeps, rather than a refusal after 30 s.
problems.fix: In observe, when locate refuses with "No live native PID" and process_alive(attached["pid"]) is false, raise ProcessEnded, keeping the refusal's own message, so it shares dead_since and the 30 s grace. While the attached PID lives, keep it as a SessionGap. Extend test_an_ended_process_with_no_new_one_is_refused_after_a_grace with a listed="no-pid" case.

problems.description: The unconfirmed-stop message (wording taken verbatim from the assignment) tells the operator to run `claude attach <id>`. Claude Code 2.1.281's `claude attach` wakes a session it finds without a handle: on ENOJOB it prints "Waking session <id>…" and restarts it, unless the state is failed. A stop stays unconfirmed when `claude stop` already ran but termination was not established yet (pipeline.stop_session raises 'termination is not established'). In that state, following the advice restarts the stopped worker. The controller's retry then finds the row under a new PID and blocks with 'Native <node> session identity changed after stop intent; reconcile manually'. The RUNBOOK repeats the advice.
problems.failure_scenario: The freeze writes ui.stop.json {stopped:false} and runs `claude stop`. The next listing still shows the PID for a moment, so the stop raises and stays unconfirmed. attach-one prints '… Inspect it with `claude logs <id>` or `claude attach <id>`.' The operator runs `claude attach <id>` after the process is gone, and it prints 'Waking session <id>…' and restarts it. On resume, stop_session sees a matching row with a new PID and blocks the run.
problems.fix: Qualify the attach advice, e.g. 'Inspect it with `claude logs <id>`, or `claude attach <id>` while `claude agents` still lists it with a PID (on a stopped session it would restart it).' Mirror the caveat in the RUNBOOK sentence. Alternatively, print the attach hint only when the current row has a live PID.

recheck.notes:
Round-1 P2 is fixed. In observe (workflow/interactive.py:522-529), once the id was attached and its attached PID has ended, a successful listing without the id now raises ProcessEnded("Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart"). attach_one waits that out with the dead-PID row under the same dead_since grace (30 s) and refuses only afterwards. Respawn case E (exit 0 or 1, then [], then the new PID) reattaches the same id. The vanished-after-grace refusal is tested: none, both, and exit 0/1. The first-attach and terminal-state refusals are still immediate. The RUNBOOK refusal list matches. I confirmed the new tests fail on f6db1f1 and on 2834604.

The fix also matters beyond the attach-ends-in-respawn path. The daemon never respawns a session with a client attached (respawnIfIdleStale checks attachers.size>0). So the common real case is attach-one sitting in its backoff or listing retries when the ~15 s prewarm burst respawns the idle lane. It then sees a `done` row omitted, or a working row without a PID, while the attached PID is dead. Before this commit, the omitted-row form was refused at once.

Guarantees checked:
- Nothing is attached without a verified live row: observe → locate → process_alive, plus a stop re-check right before `claude attach`.
- attach-one never launches or stops anything. pipeline.stop_session is the only `claude stop` path, and it writes the marker first.
- Every wait is bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT or the 30 s grace. A crash-loop reattach also stays bounded, because failures are only reset by an attach that held 60 s.
- `attached` is always set before `failures` increments, so the give-up message cannot raise KeyError.
- The confirmed-stop message is unchanged. The unconfirmed one matches the wording given in the assignment.
- Callers of recorded_stop, observe and attach_one are all inside interactive.py; main is the only entry point.
- No overlap with the areas of fix/bg-settings, fix/review-wait or fix/lane-repair.

Minor, not filed:
- RUNBOOK says the update "respawns each idle session"; really only idle sessions with no client attached, so a pane that reattached within ~15 s keeps its PID.
- If a respawn happens between observe and `claude attach`, the client reaches the new process through ERESPAWNING retries while `attached["pid"]` is stale, so the operator's next Ctrl+Z is taken for a respawn and reattached once.
- The ProcessEnded wait prints "does not list … yet" even when the row still lists the dead PID.
- Merge caveat for fix/lane-repair: if `workflow repair` rewrites <node>.interactive.json with a new background_id while attach-one runs, observe would locate the new id and treat its PID change as a respawn.
